To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) international comparisons of productivity are useful and feasible; (2) the most appropriate method for international comparisons of agricultural productivity is the stochastic production frontier; (3) this method requires a consistent and reliable data set that includes both inputs and outputs; (4) the data set should include both price and quantity data; and (5) the data set must be comparable across countries

(a) there is no unique way to compare agricultural productivity across countries, (b) the choice of a measure of productivity and efficiency depends on the purpose of the comparison, (c) the choice of the measure also depends on the data available, and (d) a consistent data set that includes information on the production technologies, the input prices, and the output quantities of all countries is needed to compare the productivity levels and growth rates across countries.
the most useful measures of productivity and efficiency are those that use the most appropriate functional form and that are based on the most appropriate data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) What is the appropriate methodology for measuring international productivity differences? (2) What are the implications of the various methods for measuring productivity differences for the competitiveness of U.S. agriculture? (3) What are the data requirements for implementing the various measures?
the measurement of agricultural productivity, its determinants, and its relationship to agricultural competitiveness.
the development of methods for international comparisons of agricultural productivity and efficiency, and their usefulness in policy and trade analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is no single best method to compare productivity and efficiency among different countries, but that the methods that we discuss in this paper provide useful and interesting information about the relative efficiency of countries' agriculture.
the methods for international comparisons of agricultural productivity are still under development, but the current methods are useful for many purposes.
there is a great need for further research on the measurement of productivity and competitiveness in agriculture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
while international productivity comparisons have been made, the data are often of questionable reliability, the measures are not well defined and the results are not well documented.
the measurement of agricultural productivity and efficiency across countries is possible but that it requires a great deal of care.
while there has been much progress in the development of productivity measures and in the use of them in economic research, the international comparisons have been less satisfactory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
international productivity comparisons can be done, and are important, but that the data needs are great.
the data needs to make such comparisons are substantial and the current data sets do not meet these needs.
there are a number of ways to compare productivity across countries, but the most useful measures are those that are most comparable to the ones used to evaluate competitiveness in the world market.
